newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London off slightly, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London off slightly, trade thin.

text.p: Japanese shares trading in London were marginally lower on Friday in thin volume with some demand in the morning giving way to selling in the afternoon as the Dow suffered, traders said.
"People were bullish this morning, but it is a different picture this afternoon," said one trader.
The Nikkei/ISE 50 index lost 0.16 point to 1,687.88. It reached the day's high of 1,693.51 early, only to come down after Wall Street opened and the yen recovered from earlier pressure.
By 1450 GMT the Dow industrials had tumbled over 75 points, rattled by the weakening dollar and the inability of the bonds to rise after benign inflation data.
The trader said the weakening yen had provoked particularly heavy selling in electric goods maker Sony Corp and car tire maker Bridgestone Corp.
By 1450 GMT Sony was down to 11,775 yen from its Tokyo close of 11,900, while Bridgestone fell to 2,865 yen in London after closing in Japan at 2,890 yen.
One trader pointed to Matsushita electric works as one of the day's prime gainers. It rose to 1,412.5 yen after closing in Tokyo at 1,370 yen.

Earlier in the day Nomura Securities upgraded the stock to a "1" rating from a "2", showing that the Bank expected the shares to outperform the key 225-share Nikkei average by more than 10 percent over the next six months.
The dollar rose to the day's highs around the 118 yen area, but weakened later to just over 117 yen.
